claims.text: Adding 2–5 at.% Al or Si to CoCrFeMnNi enhances high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Al or Si additions promote in situ nucleation and growth of continuous protective Al2O3 or SiO2 scales.
Al2O3 or SiO2 scales are slow-growing diffusion barriers against oxygen ingress.
Reactive Al or Si segregates to the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface-segregated Al or Si preferentially reacts with oxygen.
The resulting Al2O3 or SiO2 layers are slow-growing, adherent, and continuous.
Continuous Al2O3 or SiO2 layers retard oxygen diffusion into the alloy bulk.
Retarding oxygen ingress preserves the microstructural integrity of CoCrFeMnNi-based alloys.
CoCrFeMnNi without Al or Si additions forms non-protective, porous oxide layers that permit rapid oxidation.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy typically develops porous, non-uniform oxide scales, higher oxidation rates, and more rapid high-temperature degradation.
Al- or Si-modified alloys will exhibit lower mass gain than baseline CoCrFeMnNi during oxidation.
Al- or Si-modified alloys will form thinner oxide scales than baseline CoCrFeMnNi.
Al- or Si-modified alloys will form more uniform oxide scales than baseline CoCrFeMnNi.
Al- or Si-modified alloys will retain better microstructural integrity than baseline CoCrFeMnNi.
A continuous nanocrystalline Al2O3 or SiO2 layer will correlate with reduced oxidation kinetics.
The proposed behavior should hold from 800 °C to 1200 °C under controlled oxygen partial pressures for exposures up to 1000 hours.
Reactive-element additions may affect bulk phase stability or mechanical properties independently of oxidation resistance.
